episode.title: Extend package installation and validation through Python 3.14 across Linux and Windows
episode.before: At first parent 265d8a473b5d5bf001db321b251674a120ad75da, package metadata admitted Python >=3.10,<3.13 and advertised classifiers only through 3.12. Linux and Windows source-test and published-package-check matrices covered 3.10-3.12. Base dependency inputs used a single scipy<1.16 constraint, the help input used numpy<2, and the generated base requirements pinned NumPy 1.26.4 and SciPy 1.15.3 without interpreter-specific alternatives or the Python 3.13+ audioop compatibility package.
episode.after: At merge commit 861a1e4d154f268547a06497cc380e5a5dc8483a, package metadata admits Python >=3.10,<3.15 and advertises 3.13 and 3.14. Dedicated compatibility inputs select NumPy and SciPy ranges by interpreter version and add audioop-lts for Python >=3.13; the compilation pipeline preserves these markers in the generated base requirements instead of replacing them with one resolved pin. The help dependency input is aligned with the new NumPy split and explicitly requires a compatible Torch floor. Linux and Windows source-test matrices and published-package installation checks cover every supported interpreter from 3.10 through 3.14.
episode.diff: The implementation changed 15 files with 56 insertions and 42 deletions. It widened requires-python and classifiers; added requirements/python-compat.in and requirements/pydub.in; included the compatibility input from the base requirements; changed the compilation post-processing to remove resolved tree-sitter, NumPy, and SciPy pins before appending maintained marker-based compatibility inputs; regenerated base, common, browser, development, and help requirement artifacts; and expanded four Linux/Windows CI matrices from 3.10-3.12 to 3.10-3.14. No repository test file was changed, and the evidence bundle contains no status-check results.

evidence_units.claim: The pinned merge commit resolves PR #4899, has first parent 265d8a473b5d5bf001db321b251674a120ad75da, and records the resolution as adding Python 3.13 and 3.14 support.
evidence_units.source: git show --format=fuller --stat 861a1e4d154f268547a06497cc380e5a5dc8483a; issue-bundle.json linked_pull_requests[0] and commit_show_stat

evidence_units.claim: The package contract changed from requires-python >=3.10,<3.13 with classifiers through 3.12 to >=3.10,<3.15 with added 3.13 and 3.14 classifiers.

The new compatibility input partitions NumPy and SciPy constraints at Python 3.11: older interpreters retain pre-2 NumPy and pre-1.16 SciPy, while newer interpreters receive ranges that include Python 3.14-capable releases.
A separate compatibility input adds audioop-lts>=0.2.2 only for Python >=3.13, with a comment identifying it as removable when upstream support lands.
The base dependency input now includes python-compat.in, making its interpreter-specific constraints part of normal base dependency resolution.

The dependency compilation script filters resolved tree-sitter, NumPy, and SciPy assignments from the temporary base lock and appends the maintained tree-sitter, Python-compatibility, and audio compatibility inputs to requirements.txt.
evidence_units.source: git show 861a1e4d154f268547a06497cc380e5a5dc8483a:scripts/pip-compile.sh, base compilation and grep/cat pipeline

evidence_units.claim: The generated base requirements replaced unconditional NumPy and SciPy pins with interpreter markers and included audioop-lts for Python >=3.13.

The help dependency input adopted the same interpreter-specific NumPy split, added torch>=2.3.0, retained interpreter-specific scikit-learn constraints, and its compiled artifact was regenerated with newer compatible NumPy and SciPy selections.
Ubuntu and Windows source-test workflows now create jobs for Python 3.10, 3.11, 3.12, 3.13, and 3.14; each job installs the package and runs pytest.
Scheduled Linux and Windows published-package checks now install aider-chat and compare its reported version with the latest release tag on Python 3.10 through 3.14.
The complete first-parent patch passes Git whitespace-error validation.
evidence_units.source: git diff --check 265d8a473b5d5bf001db321b251674a120ad75da 861a1e4d154f268547a06497cc380e5a5dc8483a returned success with no output

evidence_units.claim: No test file changed, and PR reviews and status-check results are unavailable; the checkout establishes configured validation coverage but not observed CI success.

candidate_atomics.name: align-supported-runtime-contract
candidate_atomics.title: Align package metadata with the expanded runtime range
candidate_atomics.description: Update the install-time interpreter bound and published compatibility classifiers together so package tooling and consumers see the same supported runtime range.

semantic_action.intent: Allow package installers to admit the newly supported interpreter releases while accurately advertising that support.
semantic_action.pre_state: The package excludes interpreters at or above 3.13 and advertises compatibility only through 3.12.
semantic_action.post_state: The package admits supported interpreters through 3.14 and advertises classifiers for every newly admitted minor release.
semantic_action.validation: Inspect the built-project metadata source and verify that the upper interpreter bound and runtime classifiers describe the same supported set; the pinned diff proves alignment through 3.14.

candidate_atomics.name: partition-dependencies-by-runtime-capability
candidate_atomics.title: Partition dependency constraints by runtime capability
candidate_atomics.description: Replace universal dependency pins with environment-marked ranges and add a conditional compatibility backport where newer interpreters removed a required standard-library facility.

semantic_action.intent: Keep one package installable across old and new interpreter releases whose binary dependency support and standard-library facilities differ.
semantic_action.pre_state: A single NumPy/SciPy constraint serves all interpreters, newer supported interpreters lack compatible selections, and Python 3.13+ needs an audio compatibility dependency that is not declared.
semantic_action.post_state: Environment markers select dependency ranges compatible with each interpreter cohort, and the compatibility backport is installed only on runtimes that need it.
semantic_action.validation: Resolve or inspect requirements under representatives on both sides of each marker boundary and confirm exactly one compatible NumPy range, one compatible SciPy range, and conditional audioop-lts selection; the committed generated requirements expose these marker branches.

candidate_atomics.name: preserve-runtime-markers-in-generated-requirements
candidate_atomics.title: Preserve runtime markers in generated release requirements
candidate_atomics.description: Reconcile resolver output with maintained compatibility inputs so a lock generated on one host does not collapse cross-runtime alternatives into host-specific unconditional pins.

semantic_action.intent: Produce distributable requirements whose dependency choices remain valid across the full supported interpreter range.
semantic_action.pre_state: The compilation pipeline emits single resolved NumPy and SciPy assignments selected in the compiler's environment, losing cross-runtime alternatives in the base release requirements.
semantic_action.post_state: The generated base requirements omit host-resolved assignments for compatibility-sensitive packages and contain the maintained marker-based alternatives plus the conditional backport.
semantic_action.validation: Run the compilation pipeline, then assert that the final base requirements contain the marker-based alternatives and no unconditional NumPy or SciPy assignment; the committed script and regenerated artifact demonstrate this transformation.

candidate_atomics.name: expand-cross-platform-runtime-validation
candidate_atomics.title: Expand cross-platform validation to every supported runtime
candidate_atomics.description: Add each newly supported interpreter to both source-test and published-package installation checks on Linux and Windows.

semantic_action.intent: Exercise source installation, the test suite, and released-package installation across every advertised interpreter on both supported CI operating-system families.
semantic_action.pre_state: Automated source and published-package checks cover Python 3.10-3.12, leaving newly admitted 3.13 and 3.14 configurations unexercised.
semantic_action.post_state: Linux and Windows matrices configure Python 3.10-3.14 for source installation and tests, and scheduled release checks configure the same range for published-package installation and version verification.
semantic_action.validation: For each operating system and supported interpreter, require source installation followed by pytest and published-package installation followed by release-version comparison; the workflows configure these jobs, although their execution results are unavailable in the evidence bundle.

candidate_workflows.name: extend-cross-platform-package-runtime-support
candidate_workflows.title: Extend a packaged application across new interpreter releases
candidate_workflows.description: Coordinate metadata, runtime-sensitive dependency policy, generated release artifacts, and Linux/Windows validation when adding interpreter versions whose dependency availability differs from older supported versions.

workflow_graph.goal: Make source and released-package installation support the expanded interpreter range on Linux and Windows without breaking dependency resolution for older supported interpreters.
when_to_use: Package metadata must admit one or more new interpreter releases.
At least one dependency or removed standard-library module requires different treatment across old and new interpreter cohorts.
The repository commits generated dependency artifacts and validates installation on multiple operating systems.
anti_goals: Do not drop an older supported interpreter merely to use one unconditional modern dependency pin.
Do not claim runtime support solely by changing package classifiers or the interpreter upper bound.
Do not let a lock generated on one host replace cross-runtime marker branches with host-specific pins.
Do not broaden unrelated application behavior or optimize dependency versions beyond what compatibility requires.
not_applicable_when: The project distributes no Python package or does not declare interpreter compatibility.
All supported runtimes resolve the same dependency set and no generated artifact can collapse environment-specific choices.
The requested interpreter is unavailable in the target CI platforms or required dependencies have no viable compatible release or backport.
inputs: Current and proposed supported interpreter ranges
Direct and transitive dependency compatibility by interpreter
workflow_graph.entry_state: The package supports Python 3.10-3.12, excludes 3.13+, uses dependency constraints that cannot represent the complete old/new runtime compatibility split, and validates only the older range.
workflow_graph.exit_state: Metadata, dependency policy, generated artifacts, source-test matrices, and published-package checks consistently cover Python 3.10-3.14 on Linux and Windows, with runtime markers preserving older-interpreter compatibility.

steps.condition: The proposed runtimes are intended to become publicly supported.
steps.validation: The interpreter bound and classifiers enumerate the same expanded support range.

steps.condition: Dependency wheels, supported versions, or standard-library facilities differ across the supported interpreter range.
steps.validation: Each runtime cohort selects compatible dependency ranges, and compatibility backports are limited to runtimes that need them.

steps.condition: Release dependencies are generated through a resolver that can emit host-specific unconditional pins.
steps.validation: Regenerated release requirements retain marker branches and contain no conflicting unconditional assignments for compatibility-sensitive packages.

steps.condition: The repository supports Linux and Windows and publishes an installable package.
steps.validation: Every supported interpreter has Linux and Windows source-install/test jobs and published-package installation/version-check jobs.

validation_ladder: Statically verify that metadata bounds and classifiers agree on Python 3.10-3.14.
Regenerate dependency artifacts and verify that compatibility-sensitive packages retain mutually exclusive runtime markers without unconditional conflicting pins.
Install the source package and run pytest for every supported interpreter on Linux and Windows.
Install the published package for every supported interpreter on Linux and Windows and compare its reported version with the latest release tag.
Require observed CI status results before treating configured workflow coverage as proven execution success.
stop_conditions: Stop if any newly admitted interpreter has no viable dependency set or required compatibility backport.
Stop if generated artifacts cannot preserve the runtime-specific policy without conflicting assignments.
Stop promotion if either operating-system family lacks source-install/test coverage for a claimed supported runtime.
Defer success claims when CI execution or release-install results are unavailable.
unresolved_or_deferred: PR review discussion and status-check results are unavailable in the GitHub evidence bundle.
No repository test file was added or modified; validation is expressed through expanded existing workflows.
Actual dependency resolution and test outcomes for all ten operating-system/interpreter combinations were not observed during extraction.
The comment in requirements/pydub.in makes future removal of audioop-lts conditional on upstream Python 3.13+ support, which was not evaluated here.

unresolved_questions: Did all Linux and Windows jobs for Python 3.13 and 3.14 pass on PR #4899? The supplied bundle omits status checks.
Did the scheduled published-package checks subsequently succeed on Python 3.13 and 3.14 after release? No run results are present.
Are macOS x86 dependency constraints still relevant after the help-stack changes? The diff removes an old commented note but provides no platform validation evidence.
